diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any $s\in\rr{}$, we have \begin{equation*} M^1_{1\otimes v_s}(\rr{d})\hookrightarrow B_s(\rr{d}), \end{equation*}

issues.failure_explanation: For s<0, the weight v_s is bounded above by 1, so M^1_{1\otimes v_s} does not control the unweighted L^1 norm. High-frequency modulated Schwartz functions can have arbitrarily small weighted M^1 norm while retaining unit L^1 norm, so the displayed first inclusion is false. The conclusion is true but needs a direct estimate |\hat f(\xi)|\le \int |V_g f(x,\xi)|dx.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the inclusion with the direct estimate |\hat f(\xi)|\le \int |V_g f(x,\xi)|dx, which gives M^1_{1\otimes v_s}\hookrightarrow FL^1_{v_s}=B_s for all s.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the embedding is invalid for s<0; the lemma's statement remains true but is unsupported by the given argument.
issues.title: Invalid inclusion in Barron-Feichtinger embedding proof for negative s
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and a short local estimate fixes the proof; no substantive claim is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The product estimate is a multiplication property, for which the correct exponent relation is 1/r'=1/s+1/q, not 1/r'+1=1/s+1/q; the latter is a convolution/Young relation. With s,q in [1,2] the stated relation cannot support the claimed multiplication bound. Additionally, the proof uses |\Omega_\epsilon|^{-1/p} while the statement has |\Omega|^{-d/p}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a correct local embedding proof, e.g., via Young's inequality for the Fourier side, and correct the exponent to |\Omega|^{-1/p} or the appropriate local factor.
issues.overall_effect: The embedding and its corollaries are unsupported; the proof does not establish the claimed W^{n,r} bound.
issues.title: Wrong multiplication index and exponent in Sobolev-modulation embedding
issues.why_classification: The central proof step is invalid and the statement has an exponent error; a contained new argument is needed, but the embedding may still be salvageable.

issues.failure_explanation: For convex \Omega, \Omega+\Omega=2\Omega, so |\Omega+\Omega|=2^d|\Omega|. The correct constant is (2^d|\Omega|)^{1/p}=2^{d/p}|\Omega|^{1/p}, not 2^{1/p}|\Omega|^{1/p}.
issues.overall_effect: The convex bounds in the local FL^q approximation and Barron corollary are off by a dimension-dependent factor.
issues.title: Wrong convex scaling in Fourier-Lebesgue embedding
issues.why_classification: A one-line constant correction preserves all claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $$M^2_{v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2}}(\rr{d})\hookrightarrow M^1_{1\otimes v_{n+1}}(\rr{d})$$ if and only if $s_1>d/2$ and $s_2>n+1+d/2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only establishes the bound for f in M^2_{v_{s1}\otimes v_{s2}}, equivalent to L^2_{s1}\cap FL^2_{s2}. It does not show Q^{s2}\subset M^2_{v_{s1}\otimes v_{s2}} unless s1\le s2. Since the corollary allows arbitrary s1>d/2, the Q^{s2} alternative is unsupported and false if s1>s2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add the condition s1\le s2 for the Q^{s2} alternative or remove it and state the bound only with L^2_{s1}+FL^2_{s2}.
issues.overall_effect: The Q^{s2} part of the corollary is unreliable; only the L^2_{s1}+FL^2_{s2} alternative is justified.
issues.title: Unjustified Q^{s_2} norm in Hilbert-space approximation corollary
issues.why_classification: A local hypothesis correction or deletion of one alternative fixes the corollary.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for any $f\in M^{p,q}_{1\otimes v_{s_2}}(\rr d)$, with $0<p<\infty$

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma supplies the factor |\Omega+\Omega|^{1/p}, but the proposition states |\Omega+\Omega| (and for convex \Omega, 2C|\Omega| instead of 2^{d/p}|\Omega|^{1/p}). This can make the bound too strong for small \Omega. Also the hypothesis f\in M^{p,q}_{1\otimes v_{s2}} does not ensure the RHS ||f||_{FL^q} is finite; the proof actually needs \chi_\Omega f\in FL^q (or f\in FL^q).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate with the correct factor |\Omega+\Omega|^{1/p} (or 2^{d/p}|\Omega|^{1/p} for convex \Omega) and assume f\in FL^q_{v_{s2}} (or \chi_\Omega f\in FL^q_{v_{s2}}).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised local FL^q approximation bound is misstated; the Barron corollary's proof relies on this proposition.
issues.title: Incorrect constants and hypothesis in local FL^q approximation
issues.why_classification: Multiple statement corrections are needed and affect the guarantee's validity for small domains and the intended FL^q class.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: f(x) = C_{\sigma ,\varphi}\int_{\rr{2d}}\int_{\rr{}} \rho(x, y, \eta, b) \, e^{-2\pi ib\cdot \tau} \, V_\phi{f}(y, \eta) \,db\,dy\,d\eta,

for every $f\in M^{p,q}_m(\rd)$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that \begin{align*} \inf_{f_{N}\in\Sigma_{N}(\bb{D}_\Omega)}\norm{f-f_N}{W^{n,r}(\rd)} &\leq C N^{-\frac{1}{2}} \norm{f}{M^{p,q}_m(\rd)} \end{align*}

issues.failure_explanation: Every atom contains the spatial window \phi(x-y) with y\in\Omega. For a bounded \Omega, all atoms decay rapidly outside \Omega, so any finite sum is essentially localized near \Omega. It cannot approximate an arbitrary M^{p,q}_m function concentrated far outside \Omega in global W^{n,r}(R^d) norm. The proof uses the STFT representation integrating y over all R^d but then claims the integral is over the restricted dictionary D_\Omega, which is invalid.

failure_location.quote: \bb{D}_\Omega = \{ x \mapsto \sigma\left(\tfrac{\eta\cdot x}{\tau}+b\right) \varphi(\tfrac{\eta\cdot x}{\tau}+b-t)\phi(x-y) \text{ such that }(y,\eta, b) \in\Omega\times\rr{d}\times \rr{}\},

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Allow spatial shifts y\in R^d (unrestricted) or restrict the target functions to those supported near \Omega; the advertised global result with fixed bounded shifts cannot be repaired without major change.
issues.overall_effect: The global approximation theorem and its corollaries for Feichtinger and Sobolev spaces are false as stated.
issues.title: Global approximation with spatial shifts restricted to a bounded set is false
issues.why_classification: The central global theorem is false; no comparable version survives without abandoning the fixed bounded spatial shifts.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: |V_\varphi \sigma(x,\omega)| \;\geq\; |T_2(x,\omega)| - |T_1(x,\omega)| = \frac{1}{2\pi}\,e^{-\pi x^2} - |T_1(x,\omega)|. This implies the lower bound \eqref{eq:lowerbound}.

issues.failure_explanation: The triangle inequality gives only |V|\ge |T_2|-|T_1|, which does not imply |V|>|T_2|. In fact, at x=0, V(0,\omega)=\int_0^\infty t e^{-\pi t^2} e^{-2\pi i\omega t} dt tends to 0 as \omega\to\infty by Riemann-Lebesgue, so it cannot exceed 1/(2\pi) for all \omega. The identity-theorem argument for non-vanishing is also invalid because a single zero of an analytic function does not force an open set of zeros.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the corollary with the true statement that V_\varphi\sigma is not identically zero (e.g., V(0,0)=1/(2\pi)\neq0), which suffices for Condition (A).
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's non-vanishing and strict lower bound are false; only the trivial fact that V(0,0)\neq0 is needed for Condition (A).
issues.title: False non-vanishing and lower bound for STFT of ReLU
issues.why_classification: The stated non-vanishing and lower bound are false; no comparable version of the corollary survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using the classical complex estimate \[ |\operatorname{erfc}(z)| \le C\,\frac{e^{-|z|^2}}{1+|z|}, \qquad z\in\cc{}, \]

issues.failure_explanation: The erfc estimate is false for z in the negative real direction: erfc(-\sqrt{\pi} x)\approx 2 for x\to\infty, while e^{-|z|^2}=e^{-\pi x^2} is exponentially small. Consequently, at \omega=0, V_\varphi\sigma(x,0)=\int_0^\infty t e^{-\pi(t-x)^2}dt\approx x for large x>0, while the claimed RHS is exponentially small. The decay estimate is therefore false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace with correct decay estimates that distinguish directions (e.g., V(x,0) grows like x for x\to\infty), or remove the false bound and Remark 33.
issues.overall_effect: The decay estimate and the subsequent claim that the STFT belongs to L^{1,\infty}_{v_s\otimes1} (Remark 33) are false.
issues.title: False Gaussian decay estimate for STFT of ReLU
issues.why_classification: The stated decay bound is false for a large region; no comparable version of the estimate survives as written.
